content:
23 NOV. 2026 publication date 92 Views

As NASA’s DART spacecraft closed in on the Didymos and Dimorphos asteroids on 26 September 2022, ahead of its historic impact with Dimorphos, it returned a few precious moments of close-up views of the binary system. Since then researchers have been scrutinising this imagery to learn all they could – and attempt to predict what the European Space Agency’s Hera mission will find following this month’s arrival.

This includes an updated estimate for the size of the larger Didymos asteroid itself. Previously estimated at 780 m in diameter, the updated estimate based on detailed analysis of DART imagery is now that Didymos measures around 730 m across.

Brazil's Sugarloaf Mountain

How to visualise that size in everyday terms?

It’s about 100 m short of the height of the Burj Khalifa tower in Dubai, the world’s tallest skyscraper, or nearly two times the size of Brazil’s Sugerloaf Mountain, or around the width of the narrow axis of Zuma Rock in Nigeria.

Zuma Rock in Nigeria

The Hera science team expect to revise these size estimates to a greater level of accuracy over the months ahead, as the spacecraft ventures closer to the asteroids than its current 25-30 km distance.

Hera approaches Dimorphos

 Hera’s first images to be unveiled

In 2022 the small moonlet of Didymos called Dimorphos was impacted by NASA’s DART spacecraft to shift its orbit around the larger body. Now the European Space Agency’s Hera mission has arrived to perform a close-up ‘crash scene investigation’ of the binary asteroid system, to gather vital data to turn this grand-scale experiment into a well understood and potentially repeatable planetary defence technique.

Join the Hera team on the evening of Wednesday 25 November as they share the first close-up images of this historic transformed space object.

Hera shown surveying the Dimorphos asteroid.

Our Hera livestream starts on 19:45 on Wednesday 25 November. Follow the livestream on ESA WebTV or the ESA YouTube channel.
